model_format: Build.MANUFACTURER + Build.MODEL (no separator), as Telegram Android sends it
sources: https://dumps.tadiphone.dev/dumps -- stock factory firmware build.prop, for the ro.product.manufacturer casing and for the OPPO, realme and vivo ceilings
notes: Allowed SDKs run from the API level current at release up to min(latest, launch + 4, API level at support end).

Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO, OPPO, realme and vivo carry exactly one SDK each: the one their newest shipped stable firmware proves they run. Those brands have no release date in any public feed -- endoflife.date tracks no Chinese phone brand and Google's catalog carries no dates -- so a range below that level could not be checked against a launch version and would offer a phone a release it never ran. The measured level is listed and nothing else.

Huawei and Honor are absent on purpose -- Huawei has no Android 13+ firmware because it moved to HarmonyOS, and the Honor dumps are GSI or enterprise images reporting manufacturer=unknown with model=magic.

model is manufacturer + code with no separator, which is how Telegram Android builds it (ConnectionsManager.java). code is Build.MODEL straight from Google's catalog. manufacturer is ro.product.manufacturer as resolved on the device, not the retail branding Google prints: verified on stock factory firmware (samsung dm3q/e3q -> samsung, xiaomi houji -> Xiaomi, google komodo -> Google, motorola rhode -> motorola, oneplus op595dl1 -> OnePlus, oppo op5e8bl1 -> OPPO, realme re60c8l1 -> realme, vivo pd2073 -> vivo). OPPO and realme hide theirs behind a bootloader-selected overlay, so the value comes from odm/etc/<prjname>/build.<flag>.prop rather than from any partition's build.prop.

Neither string is what anyone sees. Telegram's server rewrites both before storing them, measured by sending values over MTProto and reading back account.getAuthorizations: 'samsungSM-S918B' comes back as 'Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra' and 'SDK 34' as '14 (34)'. The display name is this catalog's own brand + name fields, and the SDK mapping is the API level table above, so the server independently confirms both.

The lookup tolerates casing and spacing ('Samsung SM-S918B' resolves too), and an unrecognised code is still split and title-cased ('samsungSM-ZZZZZ' -> 'Samsung SM-ZZZZZ'). So the exact raw string matters for being what a real handset sends, not for how the session reads -- but every code here does resolve to a real device, which an invented one would not.
